Prevention: Destroy weeds that act as host plants around the field (e.g. some grasses on bunds)
Plant rice varieties of the same maturity date to break the insect’s life cycle
Set up light trap during the full moon period to attract large number of egg-laying adults and kill.
Conserve and attract natural enemies (e.g. wasps, grasshoppers, spiders)
Monitoring: At pre-flowering scout daily until hard dough stage
Black bug damage can cause reddish brown or yellowing of plants.
Stunting; plants also can develop stunted panicles, no panicles, incompletely exerted panicles, and unfilled spikelets or whiteheads at booting stage.
Monitor for natural enemies (e.g. wasps, grasshoppers, spiders)
Direct Control: During early infestation, raise the water level in the field for 2−3 days to force the insects to move upwards
This can cause higher egg mortality
Use soap spray as repellent (effective for only 48 hours)
Place upwind from farm and after 1-2 days collect and destroy rice bugs
Collect rice bugs from attractant baits, mash them and mix with water and use as repellent
After harvest, plow fields to remove remaining insects
Restrictions: Attractants can be used together with some insecticides
Spray in morning between 6-10 am or in afternoon between 3-6 pm
Killing natural enemies could lead to outbreaks of secondary pests
